fragments.title: pattack (patt)
fragments.body:
Attack time of pitch envelope.

Parameters:
time: number | Pattern - time in seconds

Examples:
```
note("c eb g bb").pattack("0 .1 .25 .5").slow(2)
```

fragments.title: pdecay (pdec)
fragments.body:
Decay time of pitch envelope.

Parameters:
time: number | Pattern - time in seconds

Examples:
```
note("<c eb g bb>").pdecay("<0 .1 .25 .5>")
```

fragments.title: prelease (prel)
fragments.body:
Release time of pitch envelope

Parameters:
time: number | Pattern - time in seconds

Examples:
```
note("<c eb g bb> ~")
.release(.5) // to hear the pitch release
.prelease("<0 .1 .25 .5>")
```

fragments.title: penv
fragments.body:
Amount of pitch envelope. Negative values will flip the envelope. If you don't set other pitch envelope controls, pattack:.2 will be the default.

Parameters:
semitones: number | Pattern - change in semitones

Examples:
```
note("c")
.penv("<12 7 1 .5 0 -1 -7 -12>")
```

fragments.title: pcurve
fragments.body:
Curve of envelope. Defaults to linear. exponential is good for kicks

Parameters:
type: number | Pattern - 0 = linear, 1 = exponential

Examples:
```
note("g1*4")
.s("sine").pdec(.5)
.penv(32)
.pcurve("<0 1>")
```

fragments.title: panchor
fragments.body:
Sets the range anchor of the envelope: anchor 0: range = [note, note + penv] anchor 1: range = [note - penv, note] If you don't set an anchor, the value will default to the psustain value.

Parameters:
anchor: number | Pattern - anchor offset

Examples:
```
note("c c4").penv(12).panchor("<0 .5 1 .5>")
```

fragments.title: leslie
fragments.body:
Emulation of a Leslie speaker: speakers rotating in a wooden amplified cabinet.

Parameters:
wet: number | Pattern - between 0 and 1

Examples:
```
n("0,4,7").s("supersquare").leslie("<0 .4 .6 1>").osc()
```

fragments.title: lrate
fragments.body:
Rate of modulation / rotation for leslie effect

Parameters:
rate: number | Pattern - 6.7 for fast, 0.7 for slow

Examples:
```
n("0,4,7").s("supersquare").leslie(1).lrate("<1 2 4 8>").osc()
```

fragments.title: lsize
fragments.body:
Physical size of the cabinet in meters. Be careful, it might be slightly larger than your computer. Affects the Doppler amount (pitch warble)

Parameters:
meters: number | Pattern - somewhere between 0 and 1

Examples:
```
n("0,4,7").s("supersquare").leslie(1).lrate(2).lsize("<.1 .5 1>").osc()
```

fragments.title: label
fragments.body:
Sets the displayed text for an event on the pianoroll

Parameters:
label: string - text to display

fragments.title: octave
fragments.body:
Sets the default octave of a synth.

Parameters:
octave: number | Pattern - octave number

Examples:
```
n("0,4,7").s('supersquare').octave("<3 4 5 6>").osc()
```

fragments.title: orbit
fragments.body:
An orbit is a global parameter context for patterns. Patterns with the same orbit will share the same global effects.

Parameters:
number: number | Pattern

Examples:
```
stack(
  s("hh*6").delay(.5).delaytime(.25).orbit(1),
  s("~ sd ~ sd").delay(.5).delaytime(.125).orbit(2)
)
```

fragments.title: pan
fragments.body:
Sets position in stereo.

Parameters:
pan: number | Pattern - between 0 and 1, from left to right (assuming stereo), once round a circle (assuming multichannel)

Examples:
```
s("[bd hh]*2").pan("<.5 1 .5 0>")
s("bd rim sd rim bd ~ cp rim").pan(sine.slow(2))
```

fragments.title: room
fragments.body:
Sets the level of reverb. When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'size' parameter, separated by ':'.

Parameters:
level: number | Pattern - between 0 and 1

Examples:
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room("<0 .2 .4 .6 .8 1>")
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room("<0.9:1 0.9:4>")
```

fragments.title: roomlp (rlp)
fragments.body:
Reverb lowpass starting frequency (in hertz). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

Parameters:
frequency: number - between 0 and 20000hz

Examples:
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(0.5).rlp(10000)
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(0.5).rlp(5000)
```

fragments.title: roomdim (rdim)
fragments.body:
Reverb lowpass frequency at -60dB (in hertz). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

Parameters:
frequency: number - between 0 and 20000hz

Examples:
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(0.5).rlp(10000).rdim(8000)
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(0.5).rlp(5000).rdim(400)
```

fragments.title: roomfade (rfade)
fragments.body:
Reverb fade time (in seconds). When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

Parameters:
seconds: number - for the reverb to fade

Examples:
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(0.5).rlp(10000).rfade(0.5)
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(0.5).rlp(5000).rfade(4)
```

fragments.title: iresponse (ir)
fragments.body:
Sets the sample to use as an impulse response for the reverb.

Parameters:
sample: string | Pattern - to use as an impulse response

Examples:
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(.8).ir("<shaker_large:0 shaker_large:2>")
```

fragments.title: irspeed
fragments.body:
Sets speed of the sample for the impulse response.

Parameters:
speed: string | Pattern

Examples:
```
samples('github:switchangel/pad')
$: s("brk/2").fit().scrub(irand(16).div(16).seg(8)).ir("swpad:4").room(.2).irspeed("<2 1 .5>/2").irbegin(.5).roomsize(.5)
```

fragments.title: irbegin (ir)
fragments.body:
Sets the beginning of the IR response sample

Parameters:
begin: string | Pattern - between 0 and 1

Examples:
```
samples('github:switchangel/pad')
$: s("brk/2").fit().scrub(irand(16).div(16).seg(8)).ir("swpad:4").room(.65).irspeed("-2").irbegin("<0 .5 .75>/2").roomsize(.6)
```

fragments.title: roomsize (rsize, sz, size)
fragments.body:
Sets the room size of the reverb, see room . When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

Parameters:
size: number | Pattern - between 0 and 10

Examples:
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(.8).rsize(1)
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").room(.8).rsize(4)
```

fragments.title: shape
fragments.body:
(Deprecated) Wave shaping distortion. WARNING: can suddenly get unpredictably loud. Please use distort instead, which has a more predictable response curve second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output

Parameters:
distortion: number | Pattern - between 0 and 1

Examples:
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*8").shape("<0 .2 .4 .6 .8>")
```

fragments.title: distort (dist)
fragments.body:
Wave shaping distortion. CAUTION: it can get loud. Second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output. Most useful values are usually between 0 and 10 (depending on source gain). If you are feeling adventurous, you can turn it up to 11 and beyond ;)

Parameters:
distortion: number | Pattern

Examples:
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*8").distort("<0 2 3 10:.5>")
note("d1!8").s("sine").penv(36).pdecay(.12).decay(.23).distort("8:.4")
```

fragments.title: compressor
fragments.body:
Dynamics Compressor. The params are compressor("threshold:ratio:knee:attack:release") More info here

Examples:
```
s("bd sd [~ bd] sd,hh*8")
.compressor("-20:20:10:.002:.02")
```

fragments.title: speed
fragments.body:
Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

Parameters:
speed: number | Pattern - inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

Examples:
```
s("bd*6").speed("1 2 4 1 -2 -4")
speed("1 1.5*2 [2 1.1]").s("piano").clip(1)
```

fragments.title: stretch
fragments.body:
Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

Parameters:
factor: number | Pattern - inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

Examples:
```
s("gm_flute").stretch("1 2 .5")
```

fragments.title: unit
fragments.body:
Used in conjunction with speed , accepts values of "r" (rate, default behavior), "c" (cycles), or "s" (seconds). Using unit "c" means speed will be interpreted in units of cycles, e.g. speed "1" means samples will be stretched to fill a cycle. Using unit "s" means the playback speed will be adjusted so that the duration is the number of seconds specified by speed .

Parameters:
unit: number | string | Pattern - see description above

Examples:
```
speed("1 2 .5 3").s("bd").unit("c").osc()
```

fragments.title: squiz
fragments.body:
Made by Calum Gunn. Reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter. The SuperCollider manual defines Squiz as: "A simplistic pitch-raising algorithm. It's not meant to sound natural; its sound is reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter, depending on the input. The algorithm works by cutting the signal into fragments (delimited by upwards-going zero-crossings) and squeezing those fragments in the time domain (i.e. simply playing them back faster than they came in), leaving silences inbetween. All the parameters apart from memlen can be modulated."

Parameters:
squiz: number | Pattern - Try passing multiples of 2 to it - 2, 4, 8 etc.

Examples:
```
squiz("2 4/2 6 [8 16]").s("bd").osc()
```

fragments.title: vowel
fragments.body:
Formant filter to make things sound like vowels.

Parameters:
vowel: string | Pattern - You can use a e i o u ae aa oe ue y uh un en an on, corresponding to [a] [e] [i] [o] [u] [æ] [ɑ] [ø] [y] [ɯ] [ʌ] [œ̃] [ɛ̃] [ɑ̃] [ɔ̃]. Aliases: aa = å = ɑ, oe = ø = ö, y = ı, ae = æ.

Examples:
```
note("[c2 <eb2 <g2 g1>>]*2").s('sawtooth')
.vowel("<a e i <o u>>")
s("bd sd mt ht bd [~ cp] ht lt").vowel("[a|e|i|o|u]")
```

fragments.title: density
fragments.body:
Noise crackle density

Parameters:
density: number | Pattern - between 0 and x

Examples:
```
s("crackle*4").density("<0.01 0.04 0.2 0.5>".slow(4))
```

fragments.title: clip (legato)
fragments.body:
Multiplies the duration with the given number. Also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

Parameters:
factor: number | Pattern - = 0

Examples:
```
note("c a f e").s("piano").clip("<.5 1 2>")
```

fragments.title: duration (dur)
fragments.body:
Sets the duration of the event in cycles. Similar to clip / legato, it also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

Parameters:
seconds: number | Pattern - = 0

Examples:
```
note("c a f e").s("piano").dur("<.5 1 2>")
```

fragments.title: color (colour)
fragments.body:
Sets the color of the hap in visualizations like pianoroll or highlighting.

Parameters:
color: string - Hexadecimal or CSS color name

fragments.title: adsr
fragments.body:
ADSR envelope: Combination of Attack, Decay, Sustain, and Release.

Parameters:
time: number | Pattern - attack time in seconds
time: number | Pattern - decay time in seconds

time: number | Pattern - release time in seconds

Examples:
```
note("[c3 bb2 f3 eb3]*2").sound("sawtooth").lpf(600).adsr(".1:.1:.5:.2")
```

fragments.title: midichan
fragments.body:
MIDI channel: Sets the MIDI channel for the event.

Parameters:
channel: number | Pattern - MIDI channel number (0-15)

Examples:
```
note("c4").midichan(1).midi()
```

fragments.title: midiport
fragments.body:
MIDI port: Sets the MIDI port for the event.

Parameters:
port: number | Pattern - MIDI port

Examples:

```

fragments.title: midicmd
fragments.body:
MIDI command: Sends a MIDI command message.

Parameters:
command: number | Pattern - MIDI command

```

fragments.title: control
fragments.body:
MIDI control: Sends a MIDI control change message.

Parameters:
MIDI: number | Pattern - control number (0-127)
MIDI: number | Pattern - controller value (0-127)

fragments.title: ccn
fragments.body:
MIDI control number: Sends a MIDI control change message.

Parameters:
MIDI: number | Pattern - control number (0-127)

fragments.title: ccv
fragments.body:
MIDI control value: Sends a MIDI control change message.

Parameters:
MIDI: number | Pattern - control value (0-127)

fragments.title: nrpnn
fragments.body:
MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter number: Sends a MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter number message.

Parameters:
nrpnn: number | Pattern - MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter number (0-127)

Examples:
```
note("c4").nrpnn("1:8").nrpv("123").midichan(1).midi()

fragments.title: nrpv
fragments.body:
MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter value: Sends a MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter value message.

Parameters:
nrpv: number | Pattern - MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter value (0-127)

Examples:

note("c4").nrpnn("1:8").nrpv("123").midichan(1).midi()

fragments.body:
MIDI program number: Sends a MIDI program change message.

program: number | Pattern - MIDI program number (0-127)

fragments.title: sysex
fragments.body:
MIDI sysex: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

Parameters:
id: number | Pattern - Sysex ID
data: number | Pattern - Sysex data

Examples:
```
note("c4").sysex(["0x77", "0x01:0x02:0x03:0x04"]).midichan(1).midi()

fragments.body:
MIDI sysex ID: Sends a MIDI sysex identifier message.

Parameters:
id: number | Pattern - Sysex ID

Examples:
```
note("c4").sysexid("0x77").sysexdata("0x01:0x02:0x03:0x04").midichan(1).midi()
```

fragments.title: sysexdata
fragments.body:
MIDI sysex data: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

Parameters:
data: number | Pattern - Sysex data

Examples:
```
note("c4").sysexid("0x77").sysexdata("0x01:0x02:0x03:0x04").midichan(1).midi()
```

fragments.title: midibend
fragments.body:
MIDI pitch bend: Sends a MIDI pitch bend message.

Parameters:
midibend: number | Pattern - MIDI pitch bend (-1 - 1)

Examples:
```
note("c4").midibend(sine.slow(4).range(-0.4,0.4)).midi()
```

fragments.title: miditouch
fragments.body:
MIDI key after touch: Sends a MIDI key after touch message.

Parameters:
miditouch: number | Pattern - MIDI key after touch (0-1)

Examples:
```
note("c4").miditouch(sine.slow(4).range(0,1)).midi()
```

fragments.title: as
fragments.body:
Sets properties in a batch.

Parameters:
mapping: String | Array - the control names that are set

Examples:
```
"c:.5 a:1 f:.25 e:.8".as("note:clip")
"{0@2 0.25 0 0.5 .3 .5}%8".as("begin").s("sax_vib").clip(1)
```

fragments.title: scrub
fragments.body:
Allows you to scrub an audio file like a tape loop by passing values that represents the position in the audio file in the optional array syntax ex: "0.5:2", the second value controls the speed of playback

Examples:
```
samples('github:switchangel/pad')
s("swpad:0").scrub("{0.1!2 .25@3 0.7!2 <0.8:1.5>}%8")
samples('github:yaxu/clean-breaks/main');
s("amen/4").fit().scrub("{0@3 0@2 4@3}%8".div(16))
```

fragments.title: drawLine
fragments.body:
Intended for a debugging, drawLine renders the pattern as a string, where each character represents the same time span. Should only be used with single characters as values, otherwise the character slots will be messed up. Character legend: "|" cycle separator "-" hold previous value "." silence

Parameters:
pattern: Pattern - the pattern to use
chars: number - max number of characters (approximately)

Examples:
```
const line = drawLine("0 [1 2 3]", 10); // |0--123|0--123
console.log(line);
silence;
```

fragments.title: euclid
fragments.body:
Changes the structure of the pattern to form an Euclidean rhythm. Euclidean rhythms are rhythms obtained using the greatest common divisor of two numbers. They were described in 2004 by Godfried Toussaint, a Canadian computer scientist. Euclidean rhythms are really useful for computer/algorithmic music because they can describe a large number of rhythms with a couple of numbers.

Parameters:
pulses: number - the number of onsets/beats
steps: number - the number of steps to fill

Examples:
```
// The Cuban tresillo pattern.
note("c3").euclid(3,8)
```

fragments.title: euclidRot
fragments.body:
Like euclid , but has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence.

Parameters:
pulses: number - the number of onsets/beats
steps: number - the number of steps to fill
rotation: number - offset in steps

Examples:
```
// A Samba rhythm necklace from Brazil
note("c3").euclidRot(3,16,14)
```

fragments.title: euclidLegato
fragments.body:
Similar to euclid , but each pulse is held until the next pulse, so there will be no gaps.

Parameters:
pulses: number - the number of onsets/beats
steps: number - the number of steps to fill
rotation - offset in steps
pat

Examples:
```
note("c3").euclidLegato(3,8)
```

fragments.title: euclidLegatoRot
fragments.body:
Similar to euclid , but each pulse is held until the next pulse, so there will be no gaps, and has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence

Parameters:
pulses: number - the number of onsets/beats
steps: number - the number of steps to fill
rotation: number - offset in steps

Examples:
```
note("c3").euclidLegatoRot(3,5,2)
```

fragments.title: euclidish (eish)
fragments.body:
A 'euclid' variant with an additional parameter that morphs the resulting rhythm from 0 (no morphing) to 1 (completely 'even'). For example sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0) would be the same as sound("bd").euclid(3,8) , and sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,1) would be the same as sound("bd bd bd") . sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0.5) would have a groove somewhere between. Inspired by the work of Malcom Braff.

Parameters:
pulses: number - the number of onsets
steps: number - the number of steps to fill
groove: number - exists between the extremes of 0 (straight euclidian) and 1 (straight pulse)

Examples:
```
sound("hh").euclidish(7,12,sine.slow(8))
.pan(sine.slow(8))
```

fragments.title: Pattern
fragments.body:
Create a pattern. As an end user, you will most likely not create a Pattern directly.

Parameters:
query: function - The function that maps a State to an array of Hap .

fragments.title: withValue (fmap)
fragments.body:
Returns a new pattern, with the function applied to the value of each hap. It has the alias fmap .

Parameters:
func: function - to to apply to the value

Examples:
```
"0 1 2".withValue(v => v + 10).log()
```

fragments.title: appWhole
fragments.body:
Assumes 'this' is a pattern of functions, and given a function to resolve wholes, applies a given pattern of values to that pattern of functions.

Parameters:
whole_func: function
func: function

fragments.title: appBoth
fragments.body:
When this method is called on a pattern of functions, it matches its haps with those in the given pattern of values. A new pattern is returned, with each matching value applied to the corresponding function. In this _appBoth variant, where timespans of the function and value haps are not the same but do intersect, the resulting hap has a timespan of the intersection. This applies to both the part and the whole timespan.

Parameters:
pat_val: Pattern

fragments.title: appLeft
fragments.body:
As with appBoth , but the whole timespan is not the intersection, but the timespan from the function of patterns that this method is called on. In practice, this means that the pattern structure, including onsets, are preserved from the pattern of functions (often referred to as the left hand or inner pattern).

Parameters:
pat_val: Pattern

fragments.title: appRight
fragments.body:
As with appLeft , but whole timespans are instead taken from the pattern of values, i.e. structure is preserved from the right hand/outer pattern.

Parameters:
pat_val: Pattern

fragments.title: queryArc
fragments.body:
Query haps inside the given time span.

Parameters:
begin: Fraction | number - from time
end: Fraction | number - to time

Examples:
```
const pattern = sequence('a', ['b', 'c'])
const haps = pattern.queryArc(0, 1)
console.log(haps)
silence
```

fragments.title: splitQueries
fragments.body: Returns a new pattern, with queries split at cycle boundaries. This makes some calculations easier to express, as all haps are then constrained to happen within a cycle.

fragments.title: withQuerySpan
fragments.body:
Returns a new pattern, where the given function is applied to the query timespan before passing it to the original pattern.

Parameters:
func: function - the function to apply

fragments.title: withQueryTime
fragments.body:
As with withQuerySpan , but the function is applied to both the begin and end time of the query timespan.

Parameters:
func: function - the function to apply

fragments.title: withHapSpan
fragments.body:
Similar to withQuerySpan , but the function is applied to the timespans of all haps returned by pattern queries (both part timespans, and where present, whole timespans).

Parameters:
func: function

fragments.title: withHapTime
fragments.body:
As with withHapSpan , but the function is applied to both the begin and end time of the hap timespans.

Parameters:
func: function - the function to apply

fragments.title: withHaps
fragments.body:
Returns a new pattern with the given function applied to the list of haps returned by every query.

Parameters:
func: function

fragments.title: withHap
fragments.body:
As with withHaps , but applies the function to every hap, rather than every list of haps.

Parameters:
func: function

fragments.title: setContext
fragments.body:
Returns a new pattern with the context field set to every hap set to the given value.

Parameters:
context: *

fragments.title: withContext
fragments.body:
Returns a new pattern with the given function applied to the context field of every hap.

Parameters:
func: function

fragments.title: stripContext
fragments.body: Returns a new pattern with the context field of every hap set to an empty object.

fragments.title: withLoc
fragments.body:
Returns a new pattern with the given location information added to the context of every hap.

Parameters:
start: Number - start offset
end: Number - end offset

fragments.title: filterHaps
fragments.body:
Returns a new Pattern, which only returns haps that meet the given test.

Parameters:
hap_test: function - a function which returns false for haps to be removed from the pattern

fragments.title: filterValues
fragments.body:
As with filterHaps , but the function is applied to values inside haps.

Parameters:
value_test: function

fragments.title: removeUndefineds
fragments.body: Returns a new pattern, with haps containing undefined values removed from query results.

fragments.title: onsetsOnly
fragments.body: Returns a new pattern, with all haps without onsets filtered out. A hap with an onset is one with a whole timespan that begins at the same time as its part timespan.

fragments.title: discreteOnly
fragments.body: Returns a new pattern, with 'continuous' haps (those without 'whole' timespans) removed from query results.

fragments.title: defragmentHaps
fragments.body: Combines adjacent haps with the same value and whole. Only intended for use in tests.

fragments.title: firstCycle
fragments.body:
Queries the pattern for the first cycle, returning Haps. Mainly of use when debugging a pattern.

Parameters:
with_context: Boolean - set to true, otherwise the context field will be stripped from the resulting haps.

fragments.title: firstCycleValues
fragments.body: Accessor for a list of values returned by querying the first cycle.

fragments.title: showFirstCycle
fragments.body: More human-readable version of the firstCycleValues accessor.

fragments.title: sortHapsByPart
fragments.body: Returns a new pattern, which returns haps sorted in temporal order. Mainly of use when comparing two patterns for equality, in tests.

fragments.title: layer (apply)
fragments.body:
Layers the result of the given function(s). Like superimpose , but without the original pattern:

Examples:
```
"<0 2 4 6 ~ 4 ~ 2 0!3 ~!5>*8"
  .layer(x=>x.add("0,2"))
  .scale('C minor').note()
```

fragments.title: superimpose
fragments.body:
Superimposes the result of the given function(s) on top of the original pattern:

Examples:
```
"<0 2 4 6 ~ 4 ~ 2 0!3 ~!5>*8"
  .superimpose(x=>x.add(2))
  .scale('C minor').note()
```

fragments.title: log
fragments.body:
Writes the content of the current event to the console (visible in the side menu).

Examples:
```
s("bd sd").log()
```

fragments.title: logValues
fragments.body:
A simplified version of log which writes all "values" (various configurable parameters) within the event to the console (visible in the side menu).

Examples:
```
s("bd sd").gain("0.25 0.5 1").n("2 1 0").logValues()
```

fragments.title: into
fragments.body:
Breaks a pattern into pieces according to the structure of a given pattern. True values in the given pattern cause the corresponding subcycle of the source pattern to be looped, and for an (optional) given function to be applied. False values result in the corresponding part of the source pattern to be played unchanged.

Examples:
```
sound("bd sd ht lt").into("1 0", hurry(2))
```

fragments.title: arpWith
fragments.body:
Selects indices in in stacked notes.

Examples:
```
note("<[c,eb,g]!2 [c,f,ab] [d,f,ab]>")
.arpWith(haps => haps[2])
```

fragments.title: arp
fragments.body:
Selects indices in in stacked notes.

Examples:
```
note("<[c,eb,g]!2 [c,f,ab] [d,f,ab]>")
.arp("0 [0,2] 1 [0,2]")
```

fragments.title: add
sub
fragments.body:
Like add, but the given numbers are subtracted.

Examples:
```
n("0 2 4".sub("<0 1 2 3>")).scale("C4:minor")
// See add for more information.
```

fragments.title: mul
fragments.body:
Multiplies each number by the given factor.

Examples:
```
"<1 1.5 [1.66, <2 2.33>]>*4".mul(150).freq()
```

fragments.title: div
fragments.body: Divides each number by the given factor.

fragments.title: struct
fragments.body:
Applies the given structure to the pattern:

Examples:
```
note("c,eb,g")
  .struct("x ~ x ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~")
  .slow(2)
```

fragments.title: mask
fragments.body:
Returns silence when mask is 0 or "~"

Examples:
```
note("c [eb,g] d [eb,g]").mask("<1 [0 1]>")
```

fragments.title: reset
fragments.body:
Resets the pattern to the start of the cycle for each onset of the reset pattern.

Examples:
```
s("[<bd lt> sd]*2, hh*8").reset("<x@3 x(5,8)>")
```

fragments.title: restart
fragments.body:
Restarts the pattern for each onset of the restart pattern. While reset will only reset the current cycle, restart will start from cycle 0.

Examples:
```
s("[<bd lt> sd]*2, hh*8").restart("<x@3 x(5,8)>")
```

fragments.title: gap
fragments.body:
Does absolutely nothing, but with a given metrical 'steps'

Parameters:
steps: number

Examples:
```
gap(3) // "~@3"
```

fragments.title: silence
fragments.body:
Does absolutely nothing..

Examples:
```
silence // "~"
```

fragments.title: pure
fragments.body:
A discrete value that repeats once per cycle.

Examples:
```
pure('e4') // "e4"
```

fragments.title: sequenceP
fragments.body: Takes a list of patterns, and returns a pattern of lists.

fragments.title: stack (polyrhythm, pr)
slowcat
fragments.body:
Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle: synonyms: cat

Examples:
```
slowcat("e5", "b4", ["d5", "c5"])
```

fragments.title: slowcatPrime
fragments.body:
Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle. Unlike slowcat, this version will skip cycles.

Parameters:
items: any - The items to concatenate

fragments.title: cat (slowcat)
fragments.body:
The given items are con cat enated, where each one takes one cycle.

Parameters:
items: any - The items to concatenate

Examples:
```
cat("e5", "b4", ["d5", "c5"]).note()
// "<e5 b4 [d5 c5]>".note()
// As a chained function:
s("hh*4").cat(
   note("c4(5,8)")
)
```

fragments.title: arrange
fragments.body:
Allows to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles. Takes a variable number of arrays with two elements specifying the number of cycles and the pattern to use.

Examples:
```
arrange(
  [4, "<c a f e>(3,8)"],
  [2, "<g a>(5,8)"]
).note()
```

fragments.title: seqPLoop
fragments.body:
Similarly to arrange , allows you to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles. Unlike arrange , you specify a start and stop time for each pattern rather than duration, which means that patterns can overlap.

Examples:
```
seqPLoop([0, 2, "bd(3,8)"],
         [1, 3, "cp(3,8)"]
        )
  .sound()
```

fragments.title: seq (sequence, fastcat)
register
fragments.body:
Registers a new pattern method. The method is added to the Pattern class + the standalone function is returned from register.

Parameters:
name: string | Array.<string> - name of the function, or an array of names to be used as synonyms
func: function - function with 1 or more params, where last is the current pattern

fragments.title: round
fragments.body:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values rounded to the nearest integer.

Examples:
```
n("0.5 1.5 2.5".round()).scale("C:major")
```

fragments.title: floor
fragments.body:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to their mathematical floor. E.g. 3.7 replaced with to 3 , and -4.2 replaced with -5 .

Examples:
```
note("42 42.1 42.5 43".floor())
```

fragments.title: ceil
fragments.body:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to their mathematical ceiling. E.g. 3.2 replaced with 4 , and -4.2 replaced with -4 .

Examples:
```
note("42 42.1 42.5 43".ceil())
```

fragments.title: toBipolar
fragments.body: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the bipolar range -1 .. 1

fragments.title: fromBipolar
fragments.body: Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the unipolar range 0 .. 1

fragments.title: range
fragments.body:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1. Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range. Most useful in combination with continuous patterns.

Examples:
```
s("[bd sd]*2,hh*8")
.cutoff(sine.range(500,4000))
```

fragments.title: rangex
fragments.body:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range, following an exponential curve.

Examples:
```
s("[bd sd]*2,hh*8")
.cutoff(sine.rangex(500,4000))
```

fragments.title: range2
fragments.body:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1 Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range.

Examples:
```
s("[bd sd]*2,hh*8")
.cutoff(sine2.range2(500,4000))
```

fragments.title: ratio
fragments.body:
Allows dividing numbers via list notation using ":". Returns a new pattern with just numbers.

Examples:
```
ratio("1, 5:4, 3:2").mul(110)
.freq().s("piano")
```

fragments.title: compress
fragments.body:
Compress each cycle into the given timespan, leaving a gap

Examples:
```
cat(
  s("bd sd").compress(.25,.75),
  s("~ bd sd ~")
)
```

fragments.title: fastGap (fastgap)
fragments.body:
speeds up a pattern like fast, but rather than it playing multiple times as fast would it instead leaves a gap in the remaining space of the cycle. For example, the following will play the sound pattern "bd sn" only once but compressed into the first half of the cycle, i.e. twice as fast.

Examples:
```
s("bd sd").fastGap(2)
```

fragments.title: focus
fragments.body:
Similar to compress , but doesn't leave gaps, and the 'focus' can be bigger than a cycle

Examples:
```
s("bd hh sd hh").focus(1/4, 3/4)
```

fragments.title: ply
fragments.body:
The ply function repeats each event the given number of times.

Examples:
```
s("bd ~ sd cp").ply("<1 2 3>")
```

fragments.title: fast (density)
fragments.body:
Speed up a pattern by the given factor. Used by "*" in mini notation.

Parameters:
factor: number | Pattern - speed up factor

Examples:
```
s("bd hh sd hh").fast(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]*2")
```

fragments.title: hurry
fragments.body:
Both speeds up the pattern (like 'fast') and the sample playback (like 'speed').

Examples:
```
s("bd sd:2").hurry("<1 2 4 3>").slow(1.5)
```

fragments.title: slow (sparsity)
fragments.body:
Slow down a pattern over the given number of cycles. Like the "/" operator in mini notation.

Parameters:
factor: number | Pattern - slow down factor

Examples:
```
s("bd hh sd hh").slow(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]/2")
```

fragments.title: inside
fragments.body:
Carries out an operation 'inside' a cycle.

Examples:
```
"0 1 2 3 4 3 2 1".inside(4, rev).scale('C major').note()
// "0 1 2 3 4 3 2 1".slow(4).rev().fast(4).scale('C major').note()
```

fragments.title: outside
fragments.body:
Carries out an operation 'outside' a cycle.

Examples:
```
"<[0 1] 2 [3 4] 5>".outside(4, rev).scale('C major').note()
// "<[0 1] 2 [3 4] 5>".fast(4).rev().slow(4).scale('C major').note()
```

fragments.title: lastOf
fragments.body:
Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the last cycle.

Parameters:
n: number - how many cycles
func: function - function to apply

Examples:
```
note("c3 d3 e3 g3").lastOf(4, x=>x.rev())
```

fragments.title: firstOf
fragments.body:
Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the first cycle.

Parameters:
n: number - how many cycles
func: function - function to apply

Examples:
```
note("c3 d3 e3 g3").firstOf(4, x=>x.rev())
```

fragments.title: every
fragments.body:
An alias for firstOf

Parameters:
n: number - how many cycles
func: function - function to apply

Examples:
```
note("c3 d3 e3 g3").every(4, x=>x.rev())
```

fragments.title: apply
fragments.body:
Like layer, but with a single function:

Examples:
```
"<c3 eb3 g3>".scale('C minor').apply(scaleTranspose("0,2,4")).note()
```

fragments.title: cpm
fragments.body:
Plays the pattern at the given cycles per minute.

Examples:
```
s("<bd sd>,hh*2").cpm(90) // = 90 bpm
```

fragments.title: early
fragments.body:
Nudge a pattern to start earlier in time. Equivalent of Tidal's <~ operator

Parameters:
cycles: number | Pattern - number of cycles to nudge left

Examples:
```
"bd ~".stack("hh ~".early(.1)).s()
```

fragments.title: late
fragments.body:
Nudge a pattern to start later in time. Equivalent of Tidal's ~> operator

Parameters:
cycles: number | Pattern - number of cycles to nudge right

Examples:
```
"bd ~".stack("hh ~".late(.1)).s()
```

fragments.title: zoom
fragments.body:
Plays a portion of a pattern, specified by the beginning and end of a time span. The new resulting pattern is played over the time period of the original pattern:

Examples:
```
s("bd*2 hh*3 [sd bd]*2 perc").zoom(0.25, 0.75)
// s("hh*3 [sd bd]*2") // equivalent
```

fragments.title: bite
fragments.body:
Splits a pattern into the given number of slices, and plays them according to a pattern of slice numbers. Similar to slice , but slices up patterns rather than sound samples.

Parameters:
number: number - of slices
slices: number - to play

Examples:
```
note("0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7".scale('c:mixolydian'))
.bite(4, "3 2 1 0")
sound("bd - bd bd*2, - sd:6 - sd:5 sd:1 - [- sd:2] -, hh [- cp:7]")
  .bank("RolandTR909").speed(1.2)
  .bite(4, "0 0 [1 2] <3 2> 0 0 [2 1] 3")
```

fragments.title: linger
fragments.body:
Selects the given fraction of the pattern and repeats that part to fill the remainder of the cycle.

Parameters:
fraction: number - fraction to select

Examples:
```
s("lt ht mt cp, [hh oh]*2").linger("<1 .5 .25 .125>")
```

fragments.title: segment (seg)
fragments.body:
Samples the pattern at a rate of n events per cycle. Useful for turning a continuous pattern into a discrete one.

Parameters:
segments: number - number of segments per cycle

Examples:
```
note(saw.range(40,52).segment(24))
```

fragments.title: swingBy
fragments.body:
The function swingBy x n breaks each cycle into n slices, and then delays events in the second half of each slice by the amount x , which is relative to the size of the (half) slice. So if x is 0 it does nothing, 0.5 delays for half the note duration, and 1 will wrap around to doing nothing again. The end result is a shuffle or swing-like rhythm

Parameters:
subdivision: number
offset: number

Examples:
```
s("hh*8").swingBy(1/3, 4)
```

fragments.title: swing
fragments.body:
Shorthand for swingBy with 1/3:

Parameters:
subdivision: number

Examples:
```
s("hh*8").swing(4)
// s("hh*8").swingBy(1/3, 4)
```

fragments.title: invert (inv)
fragments.body:
Swaps 1s and 0s in a binary pattern.

Examples:
```
s("bd").struct("1 0 0 1 0 0 1 0".lastOf(4, invert))
```

fragments.title: when
fragments.body:
Applies the given function whenever the given pattern is in a true state.

Parameters:
binary_pat: Pattern
func: function

Examples:
```
"c3 eb3 g3".when("<0 1>/2", x=>x.sub("5")).note()
```

fragments.title: off
fragments.body:
Superimposes the function result on top of the original pattern, delayed by the given time.

Parameters:
time: Pattern | number - offset time
func: function - function to apply

Examples:
```
"c3 eb3 g3".off(1/8, x=>x.add(7)).note()
```

fragments.title: brak
fragments.body: Returns a new pattern where every other cycle is played once, twice as fast, and offset in time by one quarter of a cycle. Creates a kind of breakbeat feel.

fragments.title: rev
fragments.body:
Reverse all haps in a pattern

Examples:
```
note("c d e g").rev()
```

fragments.title: pressBy
fragments.body:
Like press, but allows you to specify the amount by which each event is shifted. pressBy(0.5) is the same as press, while pressBy(1/3) shifts each event by a third of its timespan.

Examples:
```
stack(s("hh*4"),
      s("bd mt sd ht").pressBy("<0 0.5 0.25>")
     ).slow(2)
```

fragments.title: press
fragments.body:
Syncopates a rhythm, by shifting each event halfway into its timespan.

Examples:
```
stack(s("hh*4"),
      s("bd mt sd ht").every(4, press)
     ).slow(2)
```

fragments.title: hush
fragments.body:
Silences a pattern.

Examples:
```
stack(
  s("bd").hush(),
  s("hh*3")
)
```

fragments.title: palindrome
fragments.body:
Applies rev to a pattern every other cycle, so that the pattern alternates between forwards and backwards.

Examples:
```
note("c d e g").palindrome()
```

fragments.title: juxBy (juxby)
fragments.body:
Jux with adjustable stereo width. 0 = mono, 1 = full stereo.

Examples:
```
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxBy("<0 .5 1>/2", rev)
```

fragments.title: jux
fragments.body:
The jux function creates strange stereo effects, by applying a function to a pattern, but only in the right-hand channel.

Examples:
```
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(rev)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(press)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(iter(4))
```

fragments.title: echoWith (echowith, stutWith, stutwith)
fragments.body:
Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

Parameters:
times: number - how many times to repeat
time: number - cycle offset between iterations
func: function - function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

Examples:
```
"<0 [2 4]>"
.echoWith(4, 1/8, (p,n) => p.add(n*2))
.scale("C:minor").note()
```

fragments.title: echo
fragments.body:
Superimpose and offset multiple times, gradually decreasing the velocity

Parameters:
times: number - how many times to repeat
time: number - cycle offset between iterations
feedback: number - velocity multiplicator for each iteration

Examples:
```
s("bd sd").echo(3, 1/6, .8)
```

fragments.title: stut
fragments.body:
Deprecated. Like echo, but the last 2 parameters are flipped.

Parameters:
times: number - how many times to repeat
feedback: number - velocity multiplicator for each iteration
time: number - cycle offset between iterations

Examples:
```
s("bd sd").stut(3, .8, 1/6)
```

fragments.title: iter
fragments.body:
Divides a pattern into a given number of subdivisions, plays the subdivisions in order, but increments the starting subdivision each cycle. The pattern wraps to the first subdivision after the last subdivision is played.

Examples:
```
note("0 1 2 3".scale('A minor')).iter(4)
```

fragments.title: iterBack (iterback)
fragments.body:
Like iter , but plays the subdivisions in reverse order. Known as iter' in tidalcycles

Examples:
```
note("0 1 2 3".scale('A minor')).iterBack(4)
```

fragments.title: repeatCycles
fragments.body:
Repeats each cycle the given number of times.

Examples:
```
note(irand(12).add(34)).segment(4).repeatCycles(2).s("gm_acoustic_guitar_nylon")
```

fragments.title: chunk (slowChunk, slowchunk)
fragments.body:
Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

Examples:
```
"0 1 2 3".chunk(4, x=>x.add(7))
.scale("A:minor").note()
```

fragments.title: chunkBack (chunkback)
fragments.body:
Like chunk , but cycles through the parts in reverse order. Known as chunk' in tidalcycles

Examples:
```
"0 1 2 3".chunkBack(4, x=>x.add(7))
.scale("A:minor").note()
```

fragments.title: fastChunk (fastchunk)
fragments.body:
Like chunk , but the cycles of the source pattern aren't repeated for each set of chunks.

Examples:
```
"<0 8> 1 2 3 4 5 6 7"
.fastChunk(4, x => x.color('red')).slow(2)
.scale("C2:major").note()
```

fragments.title: chunkInto (chunkinto)
fragments.body:
Like chunk , but the function is applied to a looped subcycle of the source pattern.

Examples:
```
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")
```

fragments.title: chunkBackInto (chunkbackinto)
fragments.body:
Like chunkInto , but moves backwards through the chunks.

Examples:
```
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")
```

fragments.title: ribbon (rib)
fragments.body:
Loops the pattern inside an offset for cycles . If you think of the entire span of time in cycles as a ribbon, you can cut a single piece and loop it.

Parameters:
offset: number - start point of loop in cycles
cycles: number - loop length in cycles

Examples:
```
note("<c d e f>").ribbon(1, 2)
// Looping a portion of randomness
n(irand(8).segment(4)).scale("c:pentatonic").ribbon(1337, 2)
// rhythm generator
s("bd!16?").ribbon(29,.5)
```

fragments.title: tag
fragments.body:
Tags each Hap with an identifier. Good for filtering. The function populates Hap.context.tags (Array).

Parameters:
tag: string - anything unique

fragments.title: filter
fragments.body:
Filters haps using the given function

Parameters:
test: function - function to test Hap

Examples:
```
s("hh!7 oh").filter(hap => hap.value.s==='hh')
```

fragments.title: filterWhen
fragments.body:
Filters haps by their begin time

Parameters:
test: function - function to test Hap.whole.begin

fragments.title: within
fragments.body:
Use within to apply a function to only a part of a pattern.

Parameters:
start: number - start within cycle (0 - 1)
end: number - end within cycle (0 - 1). Must be > start
func: function - function to be applied to the sub-pattern

fragments.title: pace
fragments.body:
Experimental Speeds a pattern up or down, to fit to the given number of steps per cycle.

Examples:
```
sound("bd sd cp").pace(4)
// The same as sound("{bd sd cp}%4") or sound("<bd sd cp>*4")
```

fragments.title: polymeter (pm)
fragments.body:
Experimental Aligns the steps of the patterns, creating polymeters. The patterns are repeated until they all fit the cycle. For example, in the below the first pattern is repeated twice, and the second is repeated three times, to fit the lowest common multiple of six steps.

Examples:
```
// The same as note("{c eb g, c2 g2}%6")
polymeter("c eb g", "c2 g2").note()
```

fragments.title: stepcat (timeCat, timecat)
fragments.body:
'Concatenates' patterns like fastcat , but proportional to a number of steps per cycle. The steps can either be inferred from the pattern, or provided as a [length, pattern] pair. Has the alias timecat .

Examples:
```
stepcat([3,"e3"],[1, "g3"]).note()
// the same as "e3@3 g3".note()
stepcat("bd sd cp","hh hh").sound()
// the same as "bd sd cp hh hh".sound()
```

fragments.title: stepalt
fragments.body:
Experimental Concatenates patterns stepwise, according to an inferred 'steps per cycle'. Similar to stepcat , but if an argument is a list, the whole pattern will alternate between the elements in the list.

Examples:
```
stepalt(["bd cp", "mt"], "bd").sound()
// The same as "bd cp bd mt bd".sound()
```

fragments.title: take
drop
fragments.body:
Experimental Drops the given number of steps from a pattern. A positive number will drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

Examples:
```
"tha dhi thom nam".drop("1").sound().bank("mridangam")
"tha dhi thom nam".drop("-1").sound().bank("mridangam")
"tha dhi thom nam".drop("0 1 2 3").sound().bank("mridangam")
"tha dhi thom nam".drop("0 -1 -2 -3").sound().bank("mridangam")
```

fragments.title: extend
fragments.body:
Experimental extend is similar to fast in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count accordingly. So stepcat("a b".extend(2), "c d") would be the same as "a b a b c d" , whereas stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d") would be the same as "[a b] [a b] c d" .

Examples:
```
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - cp").extend(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)
```

fragments.title: expand
fragments.body:
Experimental Expands the step size of the pattern by the given factor.

Examples:
```
sound("tha dhi thom nam").bank("mridangam").expand("3 2 1 1 2 3").pace(8)
```

fragments.title: contract
fragments.body:
Experimental Contracts the step size of the pattern by the given factor. See also expand .

Examples:
```
sound("tha dhi thom nam").bank("mridangam").contract("3 2 1 1 2 3").pace(8)
```

fragments.title: shrink
fragments.body:
Experimental Progressively shrinks the pattern by 'n' steps until there's nothing left, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with : ), that number of times. A positive number will progressively drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

Examples:
```
"tha dhi thom nam".shrink("1").sound()
.bank("mridangam")
"tha dhi thom nam".shrink("-1").sound()
.bank("mridangam")
"tha dhi thom nam".shrink("1 -1").sound().bank("mridangam").pace(4)
note("0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7".scale("C:ritusen")).sound("folkharp")
   .shrink("1 -1").pace(8)
```

fragments.title: grow
fragments.body:
Experimental Progressively grows the pattern by 'n' steps until the full pattern is played, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with : ), that number of times. A positive number will progressively grow steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

Examples:
```
"tha dhi thom nam".grow("1").sound()
.bank("mridangam")
"tha dhi thom nam".grow("-1").sound()
.bank("mridangam")
"tha dhi thom nam".grow("1 -1").sound().bank("mridangam").pace(4)
note("0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7".scale("C:ritusen")).sound("folkharp")
   .grow("1 -1").pace(8)
```

fragments.title: tour
fragments.body:
Experimental Inserts a pattern into a list of patterns. On the first repetition it will be inserted at the end of the list, then moved backwards through the list on successive repetitions. The patterns are added together stepwise, with all repetitions taking place over a single cycle. Using pace to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.

Examples:
```
"[c g]".tour("e f", "e f g", "g f e c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)
```

fragments.title: zip
fragments.body:
Experimental 'zips' together the steps of the provided patterns. This can create a long repetition, taking place over a single, dense cycle. Using pace to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.

Examples:
```
zip("e f", "e f g", "g [f e] a f4 c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)
```

fragments.title: chop
fragments.body:
Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, allowing you to explore a technique known as 'granular synthesis'. It turns a pattern of samples into a pattern of parts of samples.

Examples:
```
samples({ rhodes: 'https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/132/132051_316502-lq.mp3' })
s("rhodes")
 .chop(4)
 .rev() // reverse order of chops
 .loopAt(2) // fit sample into 2 cycles
```

fragments.title: striate
fragments.body:
Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, triggering progressive portions of each sample at each loop.

Examples:
```
s("numbers:0 numbers:1 numbers:2").striate(6).slow(3)
```

fragments.title: loopAt
fragments.body:
Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles by changing the speed.

Examples:
```
samples({ rhodes: 'https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/132/132051_316502-lq.mp3' })
s("rhodes").loopAt(2)
```

fragments.title: slice
fragments.body:
Chops samples into the given number of slices, triggering those slices with a given pattern of slice numbers. Instead of a number, it also accepts a list of numbers from 0 to 1 to slice at specific points.

Examples:
```
samples('github:tidalcycles/dirt-samples')
s("breaks165").slice(8, "0 1 <2 2*2> 3 [4 0] 5 6 7".every(3, rev)).slow(0.75)
samples('github:tidalcycles/dirt-samples')
s("breaks125").fit().slice([0,.25,.5,.75], "0 1 1 <2 3>")
```

fragments.title: onTriggerTime
fragments.body:
make something happen on event time uses browser timeout which is innacurate for audio tasks

Examples:
```
s("bd!8").onTriggerTime((hap) => {console.log(hap)})
```

fragments.title: splice
fragments.body:
Works the same as slice, but changes the playback speed of each slice to match the duration of its step.

Examples:
```
samples('github:tidalcycles/dirt-samples')
s("breaks165")
.splice(8,  "0 1 [2 3 0]@2 3 0@2 7")
```

fragments.title: fit
fragments.body:
Makes the sample fit its event duration. Good for rhythmical loops like drum breaks. Similar to loopAt .

Examples:
```
samples({ rhodes: 'https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/132/132051_316502-lq.mp3' })
s("rhodes/2").fit()
```

fragments.title: loopAtCps
fragments.body:
Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles and cps value, by changing the speed. Please note that at some point cps will be given by a global clock and this function will be deprecated/removed.

Examples:
```
samples({ rhodes: 'https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/132/132051_316502-lq.mp3' })
s("rhodes").loopAtCps(4,1.5).cps(1.5)
```

fragments.title: ref
fragments.body: exposes a custom value at query time. basically allows mutating state without evaluation

fragments.title: xfade
fragments.body:
Cross-fades between left and right from 0 to 1: 0 = (full left, no right) .5 = (both equal) 1 = (no left, full right)

Examples:
```
xfade(s("bd*2"), "<0 .25 .5 .75 1>", s("hh*8"))
```

fragments.title: beat
fragments.body:
creates a structure pattern from divisions of a cycle especially useful for creating rhythms

Examples:
```
s("bd").beat("0,7,10", 16)
s("sd").beat("4,12", 16)
```

fragments.title: morph
fragments.body:
Takes two binary rhythms represented as lists of 1s and 0s, and a number between 0 and 1 that morphs between them. The two lists should contain the same number of true values.

Examples:
```
sound("hh").struct(morph([1,0,1,0,1,0,1,0], // straight rhythm
                         [1,1,0,1,0,1,0], // wonky rhythm
                         0.25 // creates a slightly wonky rhythm
                        )
                  )
sound("hh").struct(morph("1:0:1:0:1:0:1:0", // straight rhythm
                         "1:1:0:1:0:1:0", // wonky rhythm
                         sine.slow(8) // slowly morph between the rhythms
                        )
                  )
```

fragments.title: pick
fragments.body:
Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name). Similar to inhabit , but maintains the structure of the original patterns.

Parameters:
pat: Pattern
xs: *

Examples:
```
note("<0 1 2!2 3>".pick(["g a", "e f", "f g f g" , "g c d"]))
sound("<0 1 [2,0]>".pick(["bd sd", "cp cp", "hh hh"]))
sound("<0!2 [0,1] 1>".pick(["bd(3,8)", "sd sd"]))
s("<a!2 [a,b] b>".pick({a: "bd(3,8)", b: "sd sd"}))
```

fragments.title: pickmod
fragments.body:
The same as pick , but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value. For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the second one.

Parameters:
pat: Pattern
xs: *

fragments.title: pickF
fragments.body:
pickF lets you use a pattern of numbers to pick which function to apply to another pattern.

Parameters:
pat: Pattern
lookup: Pattern - a pattern of indices
funcs: Array.<function()> - the array of functions from which to pull

Examples:
```
s("bd [rim hh]").pickF("<0 1 2>", [rev,jux(rev),fast(2)])
note("<c2 d2>(3,8)").s("square")
    .pickF("<0 2> 1", [jux(rev),fast(2),x=>x.lpf(800)])
```

fragments.title: pickmodF
fragments.body:
The same as pickF , but if you pick a number greater than the size of the functions list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

Parameters:
pat: Pattern
lookup: Pattern - a pattern of indices
funcs: Array.<function()> - the array of functions from which to pull

fragments.body:
Similar to pick , but it applies an outerJoin instead of an innerJoin.

Parameters:
pat: Pattern
xs: *

fragments.title: pickmodOut
fragments.body:

Parameters:
pat: Pattern
xs: *

pat: Pattern

Examples:

"<a@2 b@2 c@2 d@2>".pickRestart({
        a: n("0 1 2 0"),

fragments.title: inhabit (pickSqueeze)
fragments.body:
Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name). Similar to pick , but cycles are squeezed into the target ('inhabited') pattern.

Parameters:
pat: Pattern
xs: *

s("a@2 [a b] a".inhabit({a: "bd(3,8)", b: "sd sd"})).slow(4)
```

The same as inhabit , but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list, it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value. For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the second one.

xs: *

Examples:
```
note(squeeze("<0@2 [1!2] 2>", ["g a", "f g f g" , "g a c d"]))
```

setcpm(140/4) // =140 bpm in 4/4

fragments.title: allTransforms
fragments.body: Applies a function to all the running patterns. Note that the patterns are groups together into a single stack before the function is applied. This is probably what you want, but see each for a version that applies the function to each pattern separately. $: sound("bd - cp sd") $: sound("hh*8") all(fast("<2 3>")) $: sound("bd - cp sd") $: sound("hh*8") all(x => x.pianoroll())

fragments.title: each
fragments.body: Applies a function to each of the running patterns separately. This is intended for future use with upcoming 'stepwise' features. See all for a version that applies the function to all the patterns stacked together into a single pattern. $: sound("bd - cp sd") $: sound("hh*8") each(fast("<2 3>"))

fragments.title: binary
fragments.body:

fragments.body:
Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts in random order. Each part will be played exactly once per cycle.

Examples:
```
note("c d e f").sound("piano").shuffle(4)

fragments.body:

seq("c d e f".scramble(4), "g").note().sound("piano")
```

fragments.title: degradeBy

Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount. 0 = 0% chance of removal 1 = 100% chance of removal

Parameters:

fragments.title: csoundm
fragments.body: Sends notes to Csound for rendering with MIDI semantics. The hap value is translated to these Csound pfields: p1 -- Csound instrument either as a number (1-based, can be a fraction), or as a string name. p2 -- time in beats (usually seconds) from start of performance. p3 -- duration in beats (usually seconds). p4 -- MIDI key number (as a real number, not an integer but in [0, 127]. p5 -- MIDI velocity (as a real number, not an integer but in [0, 127]. p6 -- Strudel controls, as a string.

fragments.title: pianoroll (punchcard)
fragments.body:
Visualises a pattern as a scrolling 'pianoroll', displayed in the background of the editor. To show a pianoroll for all running patterns, use all(pianoroll) . To have a pianoroll appear below a pattern instead, prefix with _ , e.g.: sound("bd sd")._pianoroll() .

Parameters:
options: Object - Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:
cycles: integer - number of cycles to be displayed at the same time - defaults to 4
playhead: number - location of the active notes on the time axis - 0 to 1, defaults to 0.5
vertical: boolean - displays the roll vertically - 0 by default
labels: boolean - displays labels on individual notes (see the label function) - 0 by default
flipTime: boolean - reverse the direction of the roll - 0 by default
flipValues: boolean - reverse the relative location of notes on the value axis - 0 by default
overscan: number - lookup X cycles outside of the cycles window to display notes in advance - 1 by default
hideNegative: boolean - hide notes with negative time (before starting playing the pattern) - 0 by default
smear: boolean - notes leave a solid trace - 0 by default
fold: boolean - notes takes the full value axis width - 0 by default
active: string - hexadecimal or CSS color of the active notes - defaults to #FFCA28
inactive: string - hexadecimal or CSS color of the inactive notes - defaults to #7491D2
background: string - hexadecimal or CSS color of the background - defaults to transparent
playheadColor: string - hexadecimal or CSS color of the line representing the play head - defaults to white
fill: boolean - notes are filled with color (otherwise only the label is displayed) - 0 by default
fillActive: boolean - active notes are filled with color - 0 by default
stroke: boolean - notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default
strokeActive: boolean - active notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default
hideInactive: boolean - only active notes are shown - 0 by default
colorizeInactive: boolean - use note color for inactive notes - 1 by default
fontFamily: string - define the font used by notes labels - defaults to 'monospace'
minMidi: integer - minimum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 10
maxMidi: integer - maximum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 90
autorange: boolean - automatically calculate the minMidi and maxMidi parameters - 0 by default

Examples:
```
note("c2 a2 eb2")
.euclid(5,8)
.s('sawtooth')
.lpenv(4).lpf(300)
.pianoroll({ labels: 1 })
```

fragments.title: wordfall
fragments.body: Displays a vertical pianoroll with event labels. Supports all the same options as pianoroll.

fragments.title: pitchwheel
fragments.body:
Renders a pitch circle to visualize frequencies within one octave

Parameters:
hapcircles: number
circle: number

fragments.title: spiral
fragments.body:
Displays a spiral visual.

Parameters:
options: Object - Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:
stretch: number - controls the rotations per cycle ratio, where 1 = 1 cycle / 360 degrees
size: number - the diameter of the spiral
thickness: number - line thickness
cap: string - style of line ends: butt (default), round, square
inset: string - number of rotations before spiral starts (default 3)
playheadColor: string - color of playhead, defaults to white
playheadLength: number - length of playhead in rotations, defaults to 0.02
playheadThickness: number - thickness of playheadrotations, defaults to thickness
padding: number - space around spiral
steady: number - steadyness of spiral vs playhead. 1 = spiral doesn't move, playhead does.
activeColor: number - color of active segment. defaults to foreground of theme
inactiveColor: number - color of inactive segments. defaults to gutterForeground of theme
colorizeInactive: boolean - wether or not to colorize inactive segments, defaults to 0
fade: boolean - wether or not past and future should fade out. defaults to 1
logSpiral: boolean - wether or not the spiral should be logarithmic. defaults to 0

Examples:
```
note("c2 a2 eb2")
.euclid(5,8)
.s('sawtooth')
.lpenv(4).lpf(300)
._spiral({ steady: .96 })
```

fragments.title: transpose (trans)
fragments.body:
Change the pitch of each value by the given amount. Expects numbers or note strings as values. The amount can be given as a number of semitones or as a string in interval short notation. If you don't care about enharmonic correctness, just use numbers. Otherwise, pass the interval of the form: ST where S is the degree number and T the type of interval with M = major m = minor P = perfect A = augmented d = diminished Examples intervals: 1P = unison 3M = major third 3m = minor third 4P = perfect fourth 4A = augmented fourth 5P = perfect fifth 5d = diminished fifth

Parameters:
amount: string | number - Either number of semitones or interval string.

Examples:
```
"c2 c3".fast(2).transpose("<0 -2 5 3>".slow(2)).note()
"c2 c3".fast(2).transpose("<1P -2M 4P 3m>".slow(2)).note()
```

fragments.title: scale
fragments.body:
Turns numbers into notes in the scale (zero indexed). Also sets scale for other scale operations, like {@link Pattern#scaleTranspose}. A scale consists of a root note (e.g. c4 , c , f# , bb4 ) followed by semicolon (':') and then a scale type . The root note defaults to octave 3, if no octave number is given.

Parameters:
scale: string - Name of scale

Examples:
```
n("0 2 4 6 4 2").scale("C:major")
n("[0,7] 4 [2,7] 4")
.scale("C:<major minor>/2")
.s("piano")
n(rand.range(0,12).segment(8))
.scale("C:ritusen")
.s("piano")
```

fragments.title: voicing
fragments.body:
Turns chord symbols into voicings. You can use the following control params: chord : Note, followed by chord symbol, e.g. C Am G7 Bb^7 dict : voicing dictionary to use, falls back to default dictionary anchor : the note that is used to align the chord mode : how the voicing is aligned to the anchor below : top note <= anchor duck : top note <= anchor, anchor excluded above : bottom note >= anchor offset : whole number that shifts the voicing up or down to the next voicing n : if set, the voicing is played like a scale. Overshooting numbers will be octaved All of the above controls are optional, except chord . If you pass a pattern of strings to voicing, they will be interpreted as chords.

Examples:
```
n("0 1 2 3").chord("<C Am F G>").voicing()
```
